Unicode is one of the ways software can convert and display the binary that computers read into the letters and symbols that us humans can read.

As for why Voat is stopping you from posting about it, there's probably an error when parsing the text boxes that you're typing in. I'll look at the current commit and get back to you.

Definitely what @TheBeautifulOne said.
You can type from a greater pool of characters with unicode. Your keyboard might be producing some characters as "confusables".

In the Unicode.org link Macdaddy5000 posted you have this at the top of the page:

Unicode provides a unique number for every character

That means that every character you see is (a part of) Unicode.

Pedantism aside, Voat is complaining that you shouldn't use certain characters in submission titles. What are those characters? ASCII (common English letters, numbers and eg. .,;:-$@") is allowed, and characters in latin1 have been allowed (at least they were a couple of months ago).

At least non-Latin letters and characters are disallowed at the moment. So are symbols and punctuation as well and that includes specifically “curly quotes” (MS Word calls them "smart quotes") and en-dashes; Wikipedia uses en-dashes (I guess) in post titles like "Bose–Einstein condensate", en-dash "–" vs hyphen "-".

There's a proposed change on voatdev that is about this exact issue.
